name: Import and Reconciliation
purpose: Define one safe observation-to-mutation architecture for official workbook sources so external evidence can be discovered, parsed, replayed, reviewed, and accepted without becoming a competing domain authority.

decisions.decision: Advanced Search, RFC and WFM use source-family adapters behind one common reconciliation pipeline.
Discovery and parsing create immutable/bounded source observations; source observations never directly mutate domain aggregates.
Authoritative mutation occurs only by accepting a proposal that invokes the owning domain command under fresh state revalidation.
Each source family owns an independent accepted chronology/checkpoint; source chronology, import chronology and business-event chronology are distinct.
Logical fingerprints are computed from canonical allowlisted source meaning, making exact replay a no-op and allowing newer identical content to update only bounded import-recency evidence.
Omission from a workbook has no lifecycle, deletion, unlinking, archival or cascade authority unless a separately accepted source-scope contract explicitly grants absence meaning.
Review/disposition operates at the smallest explainable idempotent target scope; one bad target does not force whole-import rejection unless workbook-level integrity or inseparable consistency fails.
Auto-accept is an allowlisted low-risk optimization only; terminal, hierarchy, ownership, timeframe, disappearance, empty-population and competing-attempt changes remain reviewed.
Workbook/file parsing is bounded, offline and non-executing; external fetches, active content and parser-driven domain side effects are prohibited.
Header/identity recognition is versioned and exact; fuzzy or positional inference never establishes source-field or entity identity.
